title: The Tjurkö 1 bracteate (DR IK184 / KJ 136 / IK 184), Blekinge, 400–650 CE — a Proto-Norse inscription that calls gold walhakurn, the grain of the Romans, cut on an object that is itself an imitation of a Roman imperial gold medallion
language_note:
Proto-Norse, Elder Futhark, `gmq-pro` as scandinavia-03-vimose and scandinavia-05-thorsberg-chape carry it. `gmq-pro` is NOT in ingest.fidelity.LATIN_SCRIPT_LANGS, which is correct — the inscription's own script is runic and what this record carries is a romanisation — and it is the reason the english_marker_ratio branch of classify_original governs this record at all. See original_text_note, where it refused the first version.

TWO REGISTERS ARE REPRODUCED AND BOTH ARE THE SOURCE'S: the transliteration, and the normalised Proto-Norse in which the editors' reading lives. Neither is this record's work and no third register is supplied.
date: 400–650 CE, as Runor dates it, `Urnordisk`. THE RANGE IS THE SOURCE'S AND IS NOT NARROWED HERE. C-type bracteates are conventionally placed in the fifth and sixth centuries and this record does not improve on the two and a half centuries the database gives, because it has no source that would let it.
original_text_excerpt:
wurte runoz an walhakurne ·· heldaz kunimudiu ···

Wurte runoz an walhakurne Heldaz Kunimundiu.
original_text_note:
Verbatim from the Runor record for DR IK184, https://app.raa.se/open/runor, `Inskrift` panel, read on 2026-09-06. The object's persistent URI is http://kulturarvsdata.se/uu/srdb/d3844f66-5b82-407e-8727-4cea3cf47dc6.

TWO REGISTERS, IN THE SOURCE'S ORDER AND WITH NO HEADINGS. The first line is Runor's `Runtext`, the transliteration, keeping the two- and three-dot word dividers exactly where the die cut them. The second is Runor's `Urnordiska`, the normalised Proto-Norse, where the editors' reading lives. THE HEADINGS ARE NOT IN THE CHUNK AND THAT IS NOT A STYLE CHOICE: they were written in first, as `[Runtext — the transliteration]` and `[Urnordiska — the normalised Proto-Norse]`, and ingest.verify refused the record. classify_original measured an english_marker_ratio of 0.20 against a threshold of 0.18 and classified the whole excerpt `english_rendering`, not retrieval-eligible, which derived the record as published_translation_only and failed three checks at once. TWENTY-SIX WORDS OF CURATORIAL ENGLISH WERE ENOUGH TO TURN A SOURCE-LANGUAGE CHUNK INTO AN ENGLISH ONE, and the instrument was right: a chunk that is mostly the curator's prose is the curator's prose.

THE MARGIN IS NOW THIN AND IS WORTH KNOWING. With the headings gone the ratio is 0.167, measured by calling ingest.fidelity.english_marker_ratio on the chunk rather than counted by hand — the hand count in the first draft of this note said 2/14 = 0.14 and was wrong, which is FINDING 76 in miniature, in the same session that recorded it. Both markers are the Proto-Norse preposition `an`, which is also an English function word. A shorter Elder Futhark inscription with a higher proportion of `an`, `at` or `in` could trip the same threshold with no English in it at all. Reported, not fixed: the threshold is doing its job on this record and the failure mode is hypothetical.

THE CAPTURE IS NOT BLIND AND IT IS DECLARED. This session found the inscription, read the transliteration, the normalisation and the English in one pass, and pasted from that reading. There is no independent second reading. Same declaration as record 41, browser pass 1 and southasia-05; FINDING 55 applies in full.

THE RUNES ARE CUT REVERSED. Runor records the style as `vändrunor`, mirror runes, which is a property of the object rather than of the transliteration and is recorded so that a reader who goes to the photograph can match it to the text.

WHAT DID NOT GO WRONG, CHECKED BEFORE THE RECORD WAS WRITTEN. `runoz` and `heldaz` carry ASCII `z` and not `ʀ`, which is what the source prints; the capitals on `Wurte`, `Heldaz` and `Kunimundiu` are the source's; the middle dots are U+00B7 in the runs of two and three the page shows; and the final `···` is kept, because a run of dividers at the end of an inscription is information about the object.
reference_translation:
U Heldaz wrought runes on 'the foreign grain' for Kunimunduz.

THE TRANSLATION IS REPRODUCED EXACTLY AS THE SOURCE PRINTS IT, INCLUDING A LEADING `U ` THAT THIS RECORD CANNOT EXPLAIN. The `Engelska` field begins `U Heldaz wrought runes...`. Nothing on the page says what the `U` is; it is not part of any word in the transliteration, and the Proto-Norse normalisation has no element answering to it. IT IS NOT REPAIRED AND IT IS NOT SILENTLY DROPPED. A curator who deleted it would be editing a published translation on their own authority, which is the act FINDING 55 exists to forbid; a curator who explained it would be inventing a convention. It is quoted, and it is flagged.

WHAT THE TRANSLATION DOES WITH `walhakurne`, AND WHY IT IS THE REASON THIS RECORD EXISTS. It renders the word as `'the foreign grain'` — IN QUOTATION MARKS, in the source's own text, which is an editor marking a phrase as a figure rather than a thing. The first element is Proto-Germanic `*walha-`, the word Germanic speakers used for the Latin- and Celtic-speaking peoples to their south — the element that survives in `Welsh`, in `Wallonia`, in `Wallachia`, and in `walnut`, the Roman nut. `kurn` is grain. THE KENNING FOR GOLD IS `THE GRAIN OF THE ROMANS`, and it is cut into a gold bracteate.
reference_translation_note:
The English is the `Engelska` field of the Samnordisk runtextdatabas record, served through Runor. See `translation_source` for what kind of translation that is and for the boundary of the search that stopped there.

THE TRANSLATION IS WHERE THE ROMAN CONTENT IS, AND IT IS THE EDITORS' READING AND NOT THIS RECORD'S. `walhakurne` is rendered `'the foreign grain'`. The identification of `walha-` with the Romans specifically, rather than with foreigners generally, is a philological claim this record REPORTS FROM THE LITERATURE IT HAS NOT OPENED and does not assert: the published English in front of the reader says `foreign`, and every stronger reading in this record's notes is labelled as being about the word's history rather than about this inscription.
translation_source:
Runinskrift DR IK184 i senaste (2020) utgåvan av Samnordisk runtextdatabas, Institutionen för nordiska språk, Uppsala universitet. http://kulturarvsdata.se/uu/srdb/d3844f66-5b82-407e-8727-4cea3cf47dc6

THE CITATION FORM IS THE SOURCE'S OWN, printed on the record page under 'Referera enligt följande' and reproduced here unchanged, because the reuse permission asks for exactly this shape and a paraphrase of it would not be it.

WHAT KIND OF TRANSLATION THIS IS. The English is the `Engelska` field of the Samnordisk runtextdatabas record — Rundata's own published English, in its 2020 edition, edited at the Department of Scandinavian Languages, Uppsala University, and served through Riksantikvarieämbetet's Runor interface. It is a scholarly edition's translation and it is cited as one. IT IS NOT ATTRIBUTED TO AN INDIVIDUAL TRANSLATOR ANYWHERE ON THE PAGE, which is the reason seasia-05 rejected Wikipedia's Kedukan Bukit English — but the two cases are not the same and the difference is the point: an anonymous translation on an encyclopedia has no editor of record, and this one is published under a named edition, at a named institution, with a persistent URI issued by a national heritage agency. The corporate author IS the attribution.

THE BOUNDARY OF THE TRANSLATION SEARCH. What was looked at: Runor's own English field, and the citation guidance Riksantikvarieämbetet publishes for it, which states that scholarly practice is to cite the CORPUS WORK rather than the database — for a Danish signum that is `Danmarks runeindskrifter` (Jacobsen & Moltke, 1941–42), and the record page also names KJ (Krause & Jankuhn, `Die Runeninschriften im älteren Futhark`, 1966) and, here, the Ikonographischer Katalog der Brakteaten. NONE OF THOSE THREE WAS OPENED. No claim is made about whether any is reachable, in or out of copyright, or carries a different English. runer.ku.dk — Danske Runeindskrifter, the Copenhagen/Nationalmuseet database — was reached and is alive, and was NOT searched for this inscription; its translations are Danish rather than English in the pages seen. THE SEARCH STOPPED AT THE DATABASE THAT CARRIES THE TEXT AND ITS OWN CITATION GUIDANCE, which is a boundary and not a verdict about what exists.

findspot: Tjurkö 1, Augerums socken, Östra härad, Blekinge, Sweden.
notes:
F6, and the first of Scandinavia's two re-pointed slots (ruling 73). Scandinavia stood at 2 source-language records against a floor of 4; this is the third.

WHY THIS INSCRIPTION AND NOT A LONGER ONE. Scandinavia's connection to Rome in this corpus has so far been carried by runes cut on Roman-made or Roman-derived military equipment — scandinavia-05-thorsberg-chape is a scabbard fitting of Roman style, and scandinavia-03-vimose is a bog deposit of the same character. THIS RECORD CARRIES THE CONNECTION IN THE VOCABULARY ITSELF. `walhakurne` is a compound whose first element is the Germanic word for the peoples of the Roman south, and the published English marks it as a figure with its own quotation marks. A Proto-Norse speaker naming gold after the Romans is a different kind of evidence from a Roman object in a Danish bog: it is the connection having got as far as the language.

AND THE OBJECT IS THE SAME ARGUMENT IN METAL. Runor records it as a `Brakteat (C-typ)` in `guld`. Bracteates are the Scandinavian descendants of Roman imperial gold medallions, and a C-type is the form furthest from its model. What this record puts in the corpus is one object that is a Roman medallion four generations removed, carrying a word that calls its own material Roman.

NOT DECLARED GLOSS-CAPABLE. F6 carries one gloss_capable declaration and ruling 77 spends it on CIH 541. The unexplained `U` in the published English and the quotation marks around `'the foreign grain'` are both in `reference_translation`, where the loader chunks them, so the material is in the corpus if F7 wants it.

PLACEMENT: NO GAZETTEER ID, AND THE SOURCE HANDED ONE OVER AND IT WAS REFUSED. The Runor record prints `Koordinater WGS84 — Äldsta belagda (lat, long): 56.1082, 15.6124`. PHASE2's W1 rule is absolute and older than this record: NEVER AUTHOR A COORDINATE — coordinates are read from a gazetteer via an id, and a coordinate without an id is a bug the build script should fail on. Blekinge is outside the Pleiades coverage this corpus has cached, and the only GeoNames dump in this repository is China. So the findspot is `regional` with no id and the map is poorer for it. THE COORDINATE IS NOT COPIED INTO THIS RECORD, in any field, including this one.

THE PREDICTION THIS RECORD TESTS. Ruling 78's P3: `vimose-runes` has already fallen 7 → 16 and F6 places two Scandinavian records. This is the first. If P3 holds it falls further; nothing here is gated on it.

THE SOURCE IS NEW TO THIS CORPUS AND ITS TWO EXISTING SCANDINAVIAN SOURCE-LANGUAGE RECORDS CITE WIKIPEDIA. scandinavia-03-vimose cites en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vimose_inscriptions with a translation_source of 'Kiel Runenprojekt ... as summarized on Wikipedia', and scandinavia-05-thorsberg-chape cites en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorsberg_chape. Both are seed-24 records and neither is re-curated here — nobody re-curates a record. BUT THE BETTER SOURCE NOW EXISTS IN THIS REPOSITORY, with signa, stable URIs and a stated reuse permission, and F7 or Block G should know that before it writes anything else Scandinavian.

findspot_places.name: Tjurkö, Augerums socken, Blekinge
findspot_places.note: The findspot as Runor gives it: Tjurkö 1, Augerums socken, Östra härad, Blekinge, Karlskrona kommun, Sweden. `regional` WITH NO ID, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE INTERESTING PART. The source prints a WGS84 coordinate for this findspot — 56.1082, 15.6124, labelled `Äldsta belagda` — and PHASE2's W1 rule forbids authoring a coordinate: a coordinate reaches this corpus through a gazetteer id or not at all. The pinned Pleiades dump does not cover Blekinge in any entry this corpus has cached, and the only GeoNames dump in the repository is China. So no id is taken and the coordinate is not copied. A Swedish GeoNames dump would close this and is a cheap piece of work nobody has done.

subject_places.name: walhakurne — 'the foreign grain', the Romans in a compound
subject_places.note: NO ID, AND SPECIFICALLY PLEIADES 423025 `Roma` IS NOT IMPORTED. The text does not name a place: it names a MATERIAL by way of a people, in one word, and the published English renders that people as `foreign`. persia-06-shahrestaniha refused an id for `kēsar` because an office is not a city and persia-05-abnun refused one for `Hrōmāy` because a people is not a city; this is a third step down that same line — an ADJECTIVE inside a compound is not a people, let alone a place. Recorded so the connection is visible in the placement layer as an unplaced one, which is what `regional` with a note is for.
